key_insight: Multilingual, multimodal machine-learning analysis of connected speech can accurately distinguish nonfluent/agrammatic from logopenic primary progressive aphasia in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals.
clinical_relevance: This suggests a faster, scalable assistive tool for bilingual language-variant assessment, potentially reducing reliance on lengthy specialist testing.
method: 34 Catalan-Spanish bilingual patients completed picture-description tasks in both dominant and non-dominant languages.
Speech-timing, word-level, linguistic, and image-text congruence features were extracted using PRAAT, corpora, SpaCy/CLAN, and Multilingual-CLIP.
Multiple classifiers and ensemble models were trained to separate nfvPPA from lvPPA and compared across languages.
evidence_signal: The best models reached macro-F1 scores of 93% for word-level features in the non-dominant language and 92% for the ensemble in the dominant language, with no significant performance difference between languages.
watch_item: The study is small and single-cohort, so broader validation is needed before routine implementation in diverse bilingual populations.
paper_title: Differentiating nonfluent/agrammatic and logopenic primary progressive aphasia in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals by applying multilingual multimodal machine learning to connected speech
